name: Baure
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: El acento suele tenerlo en la penúltima silaba, bastantes veces en la antepenúltima, y algunas en la última.
new_statements.translation: The accent is usually on the penultimate syllable, fairly often on the antepenultimate, and sometimes on the last.
new_statements.citation: Magio [Maggio], Antonio. 1749. Arte de la lengua Baure, in Adam, Lucien & Leclerc, C. (eds.) 1880, Arte de la lengua de los indios baures de la provincia de los Moxos (Bibliothèque linguistique américaine VII). Paris: Maisonneuve. Gramática, Cap. I 'Del Acento y Declinación', p. 1.
new_statements.locator: Gramática p. 1 (= PDF leaf 14 of the archive.org scan artedelalenguad00magggoog), Capítulo I 'Del Acento y Declinación'
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (137 leaves, Google-digitised IA copy artedelalenguad00magggoog, no text layer) and rendered leaf 14 at 100 dpi. The page image is Gramática p. 1 (the following leaf is headed "— 2 —"): title block "Gramática de la lengua de los indios baures de la provincia de Majos / Arte de la lengua Baure, escrito por el P. Antonio Magio de la Compañía de Jesus... en las reducciones de la Concepcion, S. Martin, y S. Nicolas... año 1749", then "Capítulo I. Del Acento y Declinacion." followed verbatim by "El acento suele tenerlo en la penúltima silaba, bastantes veces en la antepenúltima, y algunas en la última." The same sentence appears in both IA scanned files ( line 257; line 477). Two trivial…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Default penultimate word accent, with a sizeable set of antepenultimate words and a few final-accented ones; the source gives no conditioning for the exceptions. Modern support for penultimate default: Admiraal 2016: 76 says primary stress in compounds falls on the (usually penultimate syllable of the) locative noun stem and occurs once per phonological word.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in Maggio 1749/1880; Admiraal 2016: 76 notes that in a compound only one primary stress occurs, whereas in a possessive noun phrase both nouns carry stress.
new_statements.exceptions: 'bastantes veces en la antepenúltima, y algunas en la última' — frequent antepenultimate and occasional final accent, unexplained; later (Gramática ~p. 13) the reciprocal suffix sequence -bobo is said to carry the accent on its first bo.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (citation forms in a missionary grammar, 1749 Baure, i.e. the historical variety); 'acento' in the 18th-century Jesuit tradition = stress. Modern Baure has extensive final-vowel elision (Baptista & Wallin 1968), so surface stress position in the modern language is expected to differ from this description; the authoritative modern statement is in Danielsen 2007 (phonology ch., pp. 61–81 per Admiraal), which could not be opened.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes 18th-century mission Baure (Maggio, Concepción/San Martín/San Nicolás reductions, 1749), edited by Adam & Leclerc 1880; the modern language documented by Danielsen (Baure proper, with Carmelito dialect and the near-extinct Joaquiniano, all under baur1253) has undergone heavy final-vowel elision, so the surface stress facts may differ. Admiraal 2016 (modern Baure) independently indicates penultimate default stress at word level.

sources.citation: Admiraal, Femmy. 2016. A grammar of space in Baure: A study on the linguistic encoding of spatial reference. LOT Dissertation 425. Utrecht: LOT / Universiteit van Amsterdam. (Glottolog 546829)
sources.note: No phonology chapter (defers to Danielsen 2007: 61–81). p. 76: 'In compounds, primary stress is on the locative noun stem (usually penultimate syllable) and it occurs only once. In the complex noun phrase, however, both the locative noun and the noun referring to the Ground are stressed.' Examples with stressed syllable underlined (ewokoe'api-ye vs rapi-ye to ewokoe').

sources.note: p. 1, Cap. I 'Del Acento y Declinación': accent usually on the penultimate syllable, fairly often on the antepenult, sometimes on the final; also (p. ~13) in reciprocal -bobo forms the accent falls on the first bo.
